questions.questionText: What was the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC)?

options.text: Body investigating apartheid crimes and granting amnesty

questions.explanation: TRC (1995-1998) heard testimony about apartheid crimes, granted amnesty, and documented violations.

questions.questionText: Who chaired the TRC?
questions.explanation: Desmond Tutu, Anglican Archbishop, chaired the TRC with compassion and moral authority.

questions.questionText: What was amnesty?

options.text: Protection from prosecution for confessed crimes

questions.explanation: Amnesty was granted to those who fully disclosed politically motivated crimes during apartheid.

questions.questionText: What were reparations?
questions.explanation: Reparations included individual payments, community rehabilitation, and institutional reforms.

questions.questionText: What was the Promotion of National Unity and Reconciliation Act?
questions.explanation: This Act (1995) created the TRC to promote healing and reconciliation through truth-telling.

questions.questionText: What were the three TRC committees?

options.text: Human Rights Violations, Amnesty, and Reparation

questions.explanation: TRC had committees investigating violations, processing amnesty applications, and recommending reparations.

questions.questionText: What is restorative justice?

options.text: Focus on repair and reconciliation rather than punishment

questions.explanation: Restorative justice prioritizes victim participation, perpetrator accountability, and community healing.

questions.questionText: Why was amnesty controversial?

options.text: Critics argued it let perpetrators escape justice

questions.explanation: Many victims argued amnesty meant perpetrators escaped justice without accountability.

questions.questionText: How did testimony affect victims?

options.text: Provided catharsis and official recognition of suffering

questions.explanation: For many, testifying before TRC provided first official recognition of their suffering and dignity restoration.

questions.questionText: What role did churches play in reconciliation?

options.text: Provided moral framework, facilitated dialogue, and supported victims

questions.explanation: Religious leaders provided theological grounding for reconciliation and supported TRC process.

questions.questionText: How did TRC findings compare to international truth commissions?

options.text: Unique amnesty provisions but similar victim-centered approach
Was completely different from all others

questions.explanation: TRC drew on Latin American experiences but innovated with unique amnesty-for-truth approach.

questions.questionText: What was the TRC's Final Report (1998)?

options.text: Comprehensive documentation of apartheid violations and recommendations
Only a summary of amnesty grants

questions.explanation: Final Report documented 20,000 statements, 7,000 amnesty applications, and extensive recommendations.

questions.questionText: What was the difference between gross violations and ordinary crimes?

options.text: Gross violations were politically motivated; ordinary crimes had personal motives

questions.explanation: TRC focused on violations linked to political struggle, excluding common crimes during apartheid.

questions.questionText: What were symbolic reparations?

options.text: Memorials, official apologies, and education programs

questions.explanation: Symbolic reparations included memorials, renaming of places, and public apologies to victims.

questions.questionText: Analyze the effectiveness of the TRC in achieving reconciliation.

options.text: Provided truth and healing but reconciliation remains incomplete

questions.explanation: TRC succeeded in documenting truth and enabling catharsis, but economic reconciliation remains contested.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the TRC's treatment of liberation movement violence.

options.text: Applied same standards to ANC as government, angering some supporters

questions.hint: ANC attacks like Umkhonto we Sizwe.
questions.explanation: TRC's even-handed approach documented ANC atrocities, causing controversy among liberation supporters.

questions.questionText: How do restorative and retributive justice differ?

options.text: Restorative focuses on healing and relationships; retributive on punishment

questions.explanation: TRC prioritized victim healing and societal reconciliation over perpetrator punishment.

questions.questionText: Analyze why some victims rejected the TRC process.

options.text: Wanted prosecution rather than forgiveness; felt betrayed by amnesty

questions.explanation: Many victims, especially from 1960s-80s, felt amnesty meant no justice regardless of truth-telling.

questions.questionText: Compare South Africa's approach to other post-conflict societies.

options.text: Unique amnesty-for-truth model vs. prosecutions in Rwanda and Nuremberg

questions.explanation: South Africa's amnesty was unique; others used tribunals or prosecutions for similar past atrocities.

questions.questionText: What is the TRC's legacy for transitional justice globally?

options.text: Influenced truth commission design worldwide, especially in Latin America

questions.explanation: TRC became the model for truth commissions globally, demonstrating restorative justice at scale.
